rationale: Beat-and-raise with acceleration. Record $16B rev (+22% YoY), record $110B consolidated backlog (~50%+ semis). AI semis $5.2B (+63% YoY) — 10th consecutive quarter of strong growth. Added a fourth major XPU customer with $10B+ in orders, causing Hock Tan to explicitly say FY26 AI growth will ACCELERATE above the prior 50-60% guide. Q4 AI semis guided to $6.2B (+66% YoY). Specific forward catalysts: Tomahawk 6 (102 Tbps switch), Jericho 4 scale-across router, VCF 9.0 release, VMware VCF penetration >90% of top 10,000 accounts with multi-year deployment runway. CEO extended through 2030 — removes succession overhang. Q&A direct and expansive, no deflections. Non-AI semis the only weak spot but stabilizing.

Headline EPS miss ($1.22 vs $2.23 expected), adjusted EPS roughly flat YoY ($2.27 vs $2.29). Management repeatedly hedged: 'highly complex operating environment,' 'farmers and end consumers remain largely spot,' 'elevated global grain stocks-to-use dampening volatility,' biofuel RVO/SRE policy uncertain until year-end or early 2026. Maintained FY guide but did not raise despite Viterra deal closing. CFO admitted Viterra 'mildly dilutive' this year, grain merchandising 'weren't where we would expect.' Synergies deferred to 2026-2027. Defensive framing (flexibility, resilience, 'built to perform regardless of environment') rather than momentum-building language. Forward catalysts are regulatory-dependent (RVO proposal) rather than operational. Entering earnings with momentum into a murky spot market setup — reversal risk.

Clean beat-and-raise. Adj EBITDA $1.24B above guide midpoint; raised FY EBITDA target to >$4.7B. IET backlog hit record $32.1B (+3% QoQ), $4.1B IET orders in quarter, record SSPS orders $1.2B. $700M data center power orders YTD with $1.5B target pulled forward from original 3-year timeline. Multiple specific contract wins: Sempra Port Arthur Trains 3/4, NextDecade Rio Grande Train 4, Dynamis 1+ GW, Fervo Cape Station 300 MW, Petrobras 50-tree frame agreement, Aramco coiled tubing expansion. 3-year IET target of $40B orders articulated. Raised 2035 LNG installed capacity target to 950 MTPA. Chart Industries acquisition provides strategic optionality. Macro tailwinds (AI-driven power, natural gas structural demand) explicitly called out with McKinsey $1.5T data center capex cited. Only soft spot is oil upstream (FY26 subdued) but that's a small share and offset by gas/LNG/power strength.

Solid beat ($4.95 vs $4.53 EPS). Record $17.6B revenue (+10% YoY), record $39.8B backlog (+39% YoY), sales to users +12% with E&T +25%. Power generation +33% driven by data center recip engines — clear AI/data center tailwind. Raised FY sales expectations to 'modest growth' vs 2024. Adjusted operating margin 17.5%, slightly above expectations, and would be in top half of target range ex-tariffs. Specific forward catalyst: Investor Day Nov 4 with new long-term outlook. However, tariff headwind is material ($1.6-1.75B for FY, $500-600M in Q3 alone) and margin near bottom of target range including tariffs. Resource Industries mining coal-related softness, Asia Pacific ex-China weak, Latin America flat, price realization unfavorable. Construction Industries margin down 300 bps. Strong forward orders and backlog more than compensate, but tariff drag creates near-term P&L headwind that could cap upside in a 30-day window.

Headline adjusted EPS miss ($3.04 vs $3.11). Narrowed (not raised) FY guidance to $9.05-$9.45. Most concerning: CEO had signaled a hyperscaler deal was 'past the seventh-inning stretch' last quarter and now walked that back with a hedging baseball metaphor about 'later innings can seemingly drag out' — deal did not land as market was primed to expect. Stock comp O&M headwinds are 'offsetting much of the gross margin favorability this year,' so favorable gross margin isn't dropping to bottom line. Calpine deal guidance pushed to late February call — visibility gap. Positives exist: 96.8% nuclear capacity factor, strong public nuclear support, Maryland Conowingo 50-year agreement, Maryland CPCN options up to 1.5 GW. But a stock with strong momentum into a call where (a) EPS misses, (b) the main catalyst the market is waiting for slips, and (c) guidance is narrowed rather than raised is a textbook short-term reversal setup. Q&A tone on the hyperscaler deal was noticeably more hedged than prior calls.
